explanations.answer: His name and His Father's name
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. John says the 144,000 are people “…who had His name and His Father’s name written on their foreheads.” I know a little about having a name put on you. Mine got carved into my handle by the Millers, and I've been proud of it ever since.

That's the other crowd, friend. The beast's mark on the hand or forehead is in Revelation 13:16-17. Here the 144,000 stand with the Lamb, and what's on their foreheads is His name and His Father's name.

explanations.answer: The names of the twelve tribes
explanations.explanation: That sounds official, I'll give you that. But the verse never mentions tribes here. It says the 144,000 had His name and His Father's name written on their foreheads. Sometimes the plain answer is the whole answer.

You got it, baker. John says they “…sang a new song before the throne…” and the harps and thunder are part of the sound he hears. A brand new song, and nobody's heard it yet. I'd pay good money for a front row seat.
Good thinking, because that song does show up in the book. Moses, Israel's leader, has his song mentioned in Revelation 15:3. But the song in this passage is called a new song.

I can see why you'd think that, with all the thunder in there. But the text doesn't call it a song of mourning. John says it's a new song, sung before the throne, the four living creatures and the elders.
That's right, friend. John says, “…no one could learn the song except the 144,000 who had been redeemed from the earth.” Nobody else could pick it up. Not even if they practiced in the shower.
Close, but this one is true. The text says, “…no one could learn the song except the 144,000 who had been redeemed from the earth.” That's a pretty exclusive list, baker.

explanations.answer: They follow the Lamb wherever He goes
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. John says, “They follow the Lamb wherever He goes.” Wherever He goes, not just where it's comfortable. I once followed a runaway rolling pin across the whole counter, and that was exhausting enough.

explanations.answer: They guard the gates of the city
explanations.explanation: Gates make sense for a big scene like this, but this verse doesn't say it. John says the 144,000 follow the Lamb wherever He goes. That's the thing he tells us about them here.

explanations.answer: They rule over all the nations
explanations.explanation: That's a big job, friend, but it isn't in these verses. What John says is that the 144,000 follow the Lamb wherever He goes. Nothing more is added to that line.
Not quite, baker. John says the opposite: “And no lie was found in their mouths; they are blameless.” I'd get caught fast in that crowd, because my mustache twitches every time I fib.
Right. John says, “And no lie was found in their mouths; they are blameless.” So not one lie was found. My mustache and I are both a little jealous.

explanations.answer: The hour of His judgment has come
explanations.explanation: That's it, friend. The angel says to fear God and give Him glory, “…because the hour of His judgment has come.” He doesn't whisper it either. John says he calls it out in a loud voice.

explanations.answer: The beast has finally been defeated
explanations.explanation: I get the thought, baker. But the angel never says that here. The reason he gives is that the hour of God's judgment has come.

explanations.answer: The temple has been built again
explanations.explanation: That's a creative guess, friend. But the angel says nothing about a temple being built. His reason for fearing God and giving Him glory is that the hour of His judgment has come.
That's right, baker. The angel says, “Worship the One who made the heavens and the earth and the sea and the springs of waters.” He's pointing people to the Maker of all of it.
Almost, friend, but this one is true. The angel says, “Worship the One who made the heavens and the earth and the sea and the springs of waters.” That's the call he makes.
You got it, baker. The second angel says, “Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great…” He says it twice, like he wants nobody to miss it.
Nope, friend, the angel says the opposite. He announces, “Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great…” Nothing about rising again.
That's a kind guess, baker. But the angel doesn't say anything about forgiveness here. His news is, “Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great…”
That's right, baker. The third angel says that person “…will drink the wine of God’s anger…” This is a heavy warning, so let's take it seriously and move on carefully.
I see why you reached for a gentler word. But the angel says the wine of God's anger, not mercy. It's a heavy line, and I think it's meant to be heard plainly.
I wish that one fit, friend. But the angel's words are “…the wine of God’s anger…” It's a heavy part of the passage, and the text doesn't soften it here.
Not this time, baker. The third angel says, “Day and night there is no rest for those who worship the beast and its image…” That's a heavy thing to read, and the text says it straight.
Right, friend. The angel says, “Day and night there is no rest for those who worship the beast and its image…” So no rest, day or night. It's a heavy line, so I'll just leave it there.

That's it, baker. John writes, “Here is a call for the perseverance of the saints…” These are the saints who keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus. Perseverance means sticking with it, like keeping an eye on the oven even when you want to sit down.
Wisdom is a good thing, friend, but it isn't what this verse says. The call is for the perseverance of the saints. They're the ones who keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus.
Prayer is a good guess, baker, but that's not the word here. John says this is a call for the perseverance of the saints. Sticking with it is the call.

explanations.answer: Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord
explanations.explanation: That's right, baker. The voice from heaven tells John to write, “Blessed are the dead…” and it means those who die in the Lord from this moment on. It's a comfort after those heavy warnings.

explanations.answer: Blessed are those who rule the earth
explanations.explanation: Good try, friend, but that's not what the voice says. John is told to write, “Blessed are the dead…” and it means those who die in the Lord. Nothing about ruling the earth.

explanations.answer: Blessed are those who stay awake
explanations.explanation: That one sounds familiar, baker, but it's not in this verse. The voice from heaven tells John to write, “Blessed are the dead…” and it means those who die in the Lord from this moment on.
You got it, baker. The Spirit says, “…they will rest from their labors, for their deeds will follow them.” After a long day of batches, I know how good that word sounds.
That's a fair guess, friend, but the Spirit's word is rest. The line says, “…they will rest from their labors, for their deeds will follow them.”
Rise is a good word, baker, but it isn't the one here. The Spirit says, “…they will rest from their labors, for their deeds will follow them.” Rest it is.

That's right, baker. John sees One like the Son of Man on the cloud, “…with a golden crown on His head and a sharp sickle in His hand.” Son of Man is the name Jesus uses for Himself (Mark 2:10). A crown on His head and a sickle in His hand, and John notes both.
That's a good one to remember, but it's not in this verse. John says the One on the cloud has a golden crown on His head and a sharp sickle in His hand.
Gold is close, friend, because the crown is gold. But the thing in His hand is a sharp sickle. A censer isn't mentioned in this verse.

explanations.answer: The crop of the earth is ripe
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. The angel cries out, “…the time has come to harvest, for the crop of the earth is ripe.” Anybody who's pulled a batch out at the right moment knows ripe and ready are a big deal.
The angel does come out of the temple, friend, but the reason he gives is different. He says the time has come to harvest because the crop of the earth is ripe. Measuring isn't mentioned.

explanations.answer: The seventh seal has been opened
explanations.explanation: That's a big moment from earlier in the book, baker, but it's not the reason here. The angel says the time has come to harvest, for the crop of the earth is ripe.
Yes, baker. The text says, “…the One seated on the cloud swung His sickle over the earth, and the earth was harvested.” The angel's call and the swing go together.
Close, friend, but this one is true. John says, “So the One seated on the cloud swung His sickle over the earth, and the earth was harvested.”

explanations.answer: Clusters of grapes from the vine
explanations.explanation: That's right, baker. The angel from the altar says to “…gather the clusters of grapes from the vine of the earth, because its grapes are ripe.” Grapes, not wheat. This angel is the one with authority over the fire.
Wheat and barns feel like they belong in a harvest, friend. But the angel from the altar tells the other angel to gather clusters of grapes from the vine of the earth.
Sheaves would fit another harvest scene, baker. Here, though, the angel says to gather the clusters of grapes from the vine of the earth, because its grapes are ripe.

explanations.answer: Into the great winepress of God's wrath
explanations.explanation: That's right, baker. John says the angel “…gathered the grapes of the earth, and he threw them into the great winepress of God’s wrath.” It's a heavy picture, so I'll let the verse speak for itself.

explanations.answer: Into the fire on the altar
explanations.explanation: The altar is close by, since one angel came from it, friend. But the grapes go somewhere else. The angel threw them into the great winepress of God's wrath.

explanations.answer: Into the storehouse of the temple
explanations.explanation: A storehouse would be a calmer ending, baker, but the text doesn't mention one. The angel throws the grapes into the great winepress of God's wrath. It's a heavy scene.
Not quite, baker. The text says, “And the winepress was trodden outside the city…” This is one of the heavy parts, so I'll keep it plain.
Right, friend. John writes, “And the winepress was trodden outside the city…” So it's outside, not inside. It's a heavy part of the passage, and I'll just leave the verse as it is.
